candidates.summary: the new button-label path relies on StripBidiAndZeroWidth, which keeps U+061C ARABIC LETTER MARK, U+2060 WORD JOINER and U+180E, so the body's 'bidi, zero-width and control characters removed' does not hold for them
candidates.failure_scenario: label="Pay؜ 100" or label="a⁠b": html.UnescapeString decodes to U+061C (bytes d8 9c) / U+2060 (e2 81 a0); StripBidiAndZeroWidth's fast path containsAnyByte(s, 0xe2, 0xef) returns U+061C and U+180E unchanged, and isBidiOrZeroWidth's ranges (0x200B-0x200F, 0x202A-0x202E, 0x2066-0x2069, 0xFEFF) skip U+2060-2065; the strings.Map pass drops only unicode.IsControl (Cc), and these are Cf, so the mark reaches the rendered <a class="gno-button"> label. The helper predates the diff (base markdown.go:25) and is also on-chain sanitize's, so widening it shifts sanitize output too
candidates.verify_by: go test snippet at the head: require.Equal(t, "ab", buttonLabel([]byte("a؜b"))) and the same for ⁠ and ᠎; expect "ab", observe the mark kept. Read half: gnovm/stdlibs/chain/markdown/markdown.go:25-58
candidates.evidence: markdown.go:30 fast path `if !containsAnyByte(s, 0xe2, 0xef) { return s }`; ranges at :48-55 omit 0x061C, 0x2060-0x2065, 0x180E; printf '\u061c\u2060\u180e' | od gives d8 9c e2 81 a0 e1 a0 8e
